problem_text:
A logistics coordinator needs to assign shipments to identical cargo planes. Shipments:
* Component A: volume 42 cubic meters
* Component B: volume 60 cubic meters
* Component C: volume 46 cubic meters
* Component D: volume 60 cubic meters
* Component E: volume 42 cubic meters
* Component F: volume 58 cubic meters
* Component G: volume 40 cubic meters
* Component H: volume 68 cubic meters
* Component I: volume 43 cubic meters
* Component J: volume 66 cubic meters
* Component K: volume 55 cubic meters
* Component L: volume 52 cubic meters
* Component M: volume 57 cubic meters
* Component N: volume 46 cubic meters
* Component O: volume 54 cubic meters
* Component P: volume 40 cubic meters
* Component Q: volume 38 cubic meters
* Component R: volume 68 cubic meters
* Component S: volume 64 cubic meters
* Component T: volume 61 cubic meters
* Component U: volume 37 cubic meters
* Component V: volume 45 cubic meters
* Component W: volume 68 cubic meters
* Component X: volume 52 cubic meters
* Component Y: volume 66 cubic meters
* Component Z: volume 47 cubic meters
* Component [: volume 30 cubic meters
* Component \: volume 49 cubic meters
* Component ]: volume 58 cubic meters
* Component ^: volume 43 cubic meters
* Component _: volume 55 cubic meters
* Component `: volume 44 cubic meters
* Component a: volume 48 cubic meters
* Component b: volume 67 cubic meters

Each cargo plane can carry up to 100 cubic meters of volume. Assign all shipments using the fewest planes. Each component must be loaded onto exactly one plane, and the total volume on any plane cannot exceed its capacity.
